topic.subject: science
topic.title: Components of food
topic.scope: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, roughage, water, balanced diet, deficiency diseases, food tests

misconceptions.statement: Any substance we eat that makes us feel full is a nutrient.
misconceptions.why: Students often equate the feeling of satiety with nutritional value.
misconceptions.fix: Nutrients are specific chemical components like carbohydrates or proteins that our body needs to function, not just anything that fills the stomach.

probe.question: If you eat a bowl of plain ice cubes, have you consumed nutrients?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it makes my stomach feel full.

misconceptions.statement: All food items contain all types of nutrients.
misconceptions.why: Students often see food as a generic 'fuel' and assume every bite provides everything the body needs.
misconceptions.fix: Different foods are rich in different nutrients; for example, pulses are rich in proteins while butter is rich in fats.

probe.question: Does a piece of sugar provide protein to the body?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all food provides all nutrients.

misconceptions.statement: If a food test does not show a color change, the food has no nutritional value at all.
misconceptions.why: Students struggle to distinguish between the absence of a specific nutrient and the absence of all nutrients.
misconceptions.fix: A negative test only shows that a specific nutrient, like starch, is absent; the food might still contain other nutrients like proteins or fats.

probe.question: If iodine solution does not turn blue-black on a piece of apple, does the apple have any nutrients?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it has no nutrients because the test failed.

misconceptions.statement: Eating a large quantity of one healthy food is the same as eating a balanced diet.
misconceptions.fix: A balanced diet requires the right proportion of all essential nutrients, not just a large amount of one type of food.

probe.question: Is a diet of only milk considered a balanced diet for an adult?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because milk is very healthy and nutritious.

misconceptions.statement: Deficiency diseases are caused by germs or infections.
misconceptions.why: Students are taught that most diseases are caused by germs, so they overgeneralize this to all health problems.
misconceptions.fix: Deficiency diseases occur because of the lack of specific nutrients over a long period, not because of germs.

probe.question: Why does a person get scurvy?
probe.wrong_answer: Because they caught a germ from someone else.
